[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Frontier Work and Cryosleep[/color][/head]
Frontier rounds are long and most useful work happens in crews. A new player will learn faster and survive longer by joining an established ship than by buying one alone.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Finding work[/color][/head]
- Report to your faction over its channel in the [textlink="Radio" link="Radio"] guide. State your role, location, and that you are looking for a crew. - Ask what the ship is doing before boarding. Mining, salvage, hauling, medical support, engineering, patrol, and combat require different equipment. - Agree on pay, ownership of recovered goods, and who gives orders before departure. Use a written and stamped contract when the stakes are high. - Learn one station and one ship role at a time. Do not take command merely because a slot is empty if you cannot operate the vessel safely.
Use [textlink="Banking and Credits" link="Bank"] for personal funds and [textlink="Buying and Selling Ships" link="Shipyard"] before taking responsibility for a vessel.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Leaving a round safely[/color][/head]
If you need to leave a long shift, return to a safe station and use a cryosleep pod. Tell your crew, hand over mission-critical items or command responsibilities, then activate the pod and follow its prompts.
[color=#d9776c]Do not disconnect in a corridor, active ship, or combat area when you can reach cryosleep.[/color] An unattended character can block a job, strand equipment, or leave a crew without warning.
